title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & bump actions
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: The monolithic CI workflow has grown large and slow; lint/test/release jobs run in a single composite file which makes cache usage suboptimal and changes risky. This PR splits responsibilities into focused workflows, reduces redundant matrix permutations, standardizes cache keys across repos, and bumps a handful of GitHub Actions to reduce flaky cache misses.

Summary of changes: - Split the existing .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. Each workflow has a small, well-defined matrix and targeted runners. - Introduced a shared cache helper action (.github/actions/cache-helpers) to standardize keys and restore order of operations (setup -> restore -> install -> save). - Reduced test matrix by moving long-running integration variations behind a conditional workflow_dispatch (integration.yml skeleton kept). - Bumped actions: actions/checkout@v4, actions/cache@v4, actions/setup-node@v4, and docker/login-action@v2. - Added a light-weight CI README and hygiene checks to make future changes easier (.github/README-CI.md). - Updated package.json CI scripts and added a small script to parallelize lint across packages.

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and update triggers
- [x] Consolidated cache keys and helpers
- [x] Bumped major GH Actions (v3 -> v4 where compatible)
- [x] Kept integration matrix separate (no behavior change)
- [x] Smoke-tested on feature branch (see CI checks)

Why this matters: Splitting workflows reduces unnecessary work on push events (lint and test can run in parallel, release runs only on tags), improves feedback latency for developers, and makes cache behavior deterministic. Bumping actions addresses several flaky cache races we've observed in the last month.

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing test semantics — integration/long-running tests remain behind explicit triggers to avoid accidental cost/timeout spikes in PR validation. If we want to reintroduce some integration coverage on PRs, we should do that in a follow-up with targeted canaries.
